finding.claim: GET /users has no authentication or tenant authorization; any unauthenticated caller can enumerate user id and name for any org by supplying the org query parameter.
finding.source: req.query.org at db.js:9 (unauthenticated HTTP query string)
finding.sink: req.pg.query SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE org = $1 at db.js:9, returned via res.json at db.js:10

trace.note: Route registered with no auth middleware; the file contains no app.use auth, session, or JWT handling
org taken directly from client query string and used as the tenant filter; SQL is parameterized so no injection
All matching id and name rows returned to caller

finding.guards_checked: No auth middleware in file (no app.use). Org filter is client-supplied, not bound to caller identity. Parameterized query ($1) prevents SQL injection, so injection is SAFE. Uncertainty: req.pg is defined outside this file, and an upstream gateway may enforce auth, but nothing in this repo does.

verdict.guard_found: none. db.js:8 registers GET /users with no auth middleware, and no app.use auth/session/JWT handling exists in db.js (the only app.use-like calls are none; the only setup is express() at db.js:5 and app.listen(3002) at db.js:23). db.js:9 uses req.query.org unchecked as the tenant filter, with only a parameterized $1 placeholder, which prevents SQL injection but not cross-tenant enumeration. db.js:10 returns all matching rows. The only file in the repo is db.js, so no gateway or upstream auth is visible.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: db.js:8-10 registers an unauthenticated route that takes the tenant from req.query.org (db.js:9) and returns id and name rows (db.js:10), and nothing in db.js:1-23 checks the caller's identity or ties org to it, so an anonymous caller can enumerate users for any org. The residual uncertainty is that req.pg is never defined here and an external gateway could enforce auth, but no such control exists in the available code.
